stem: The slide says each mass-matrix entry depends on all joint positions, but its 2R example has M22=m2 l2²; what follows?
subtopic: Configuration dependence is not universal entrywise

options.text: M cannot be symmetric if one entry is constant
M can depend on configuration overall while particular entries are constant or depend on fewer coordinates
The constant M22 makes the entire mass matrix invalid
Every entry must be multiplied by θ1θ2 to restore correctness

citations.locator: Lecture 15, physical PDF page 453, printed slide 4: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
The Structure of a Manipulator's Dynamic Equations

The state-space equation
              𝜏= 𝑀Θ ሷΘ + 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ
    Where,
  𝑀Θ  is the 𝑛× 𝑛 mass matrix of the manipulator
   𝑉Θ, ሶΘ  is an 𝑛× 1 vector of centrifugal and Coriolis terms
  𝐺Θ  is an 𝑛 × 1 vector of gravity terms
•  Each element of 𝑀Θ and 𝐺Θ  is a complex
   function that depends on Θ, the position of all
   the joints of the manipulator.
•  Each element of 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ is a complex function of
   both Θ and ሶΘ.



                                                                                                           4

    𝑚2𝑙2 + 2𝑚2𝑙1𝑙2𝑐2 + 𝑚1 + 𝑚2 𝑙1  𝑚2𝑙2 + 𝑚2𝑙1𝑙2𝑐2

stem: In the Cartesian dynamics equation, what must the task effort F be paired with?
assumptions: Use a consistent definition of Cartesian/task velocity and its conjugate effort.

options.text: The task velocity whose power is Fᵀ times that velocity
Any orientation-parameter derivative, regardless of the effort definition
Joint acceleration, so that Fᵀqddot is mechanical power
Joint position, so that Fᵀq is mechanical power

citations.locator: Lecture 15, physical PDF page 459, printed slide 10: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
Formulating Manipulator Dynamics in Cartesian Space

•  Dynamic equations in joint space
              𝜏= 𝑀Θ ሷΘ + 𝑉Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺Θ
•  The Cartesian state-space equation
           𝐹= 𝑀𝑥(Θ)ሷ𝜒+ 𝑉𝑥Θ, ሶΘ + 𝐺𝑥Θ
    Where,
  ➢𝐹 is force-torque vector acting on the end-effector
  ➢𝜒 is Cartesian vector representing position and orientation of the end-effector
   ➢𝑀𝑥(Θ) is Cartesian mass matrix,
   ➢𝑉𝑥Θ, ሶΘ  is a vector of velocity terms in Cartesian space
  ➢𝐺𝑥Θ  is a vector of gravity terms in Cartesian space





                                                                                                          10

solution.justification: The generalized force or wrench must be power-conjugate to the selected task velocity; a geometric angular velocity and an arbitrary orientation-parameter derivative are not interchangeable.

optionExplanations.o1: This keeps the coordinate and effort definitions consistent.
optionExplanations.o2: Orientation coordinates can require an additional mapping and conjugate effort.
optionExplanations.o3: Force times acceleration is not mechanical power.
optionExplanations.o4: Force times position is not a power rate.

•  Here the Jacobian appearing in equations is written
    in the same frames as 𝐹 and 𝜒 , the choice of this
   frame is arbitrary.
•  When the manipulator approaches a singularity, certain
   quantities in the Cartesian dynamics become infinite.
